claim: We gave an AI 45,047 Enron emails, which wrote 214 pages about the organizations Enron dealt with; every fact cites its email.
quote: We gave an AI 45,047 of Enron's emails, and it wrote 214 pages about the companies, regulators and banks Enron dealt with. Every fact cites the email it came from.

claim: Facts expire on the date the mail shows they stopped being true; no one edited a page or fact.
quote: When the mail shows a fact stopped being true, the page expires it on that date. No one edited a page or a fact.

claim: 49,401 facts were published.
quote: 49,401facts published

claim: Steps 1-3 ran on Claude Opus 5, step 4 on Opus 5.5.
quote: The first three ran on Claude Opus 5. Opus 5.5 launched before the fourth, and with no reason not to use the latest model, we ran the fourth on it.

claim: 37 of 62,205 candidate facts quoted a sentence not found in the message and were discarded.
quote: Of 62,205 candidate facts, 37 quoted a sentence we couldn't find in the message, and we discarded them.

claim: Verification forbids content from model's own knowledge.
quote: Nothing may come from what the model knows.

claim: Audit judge was a different model, Claude Fable 5.1, on 500 random facts.
quote: with a different model, Claude Fable 5.1, as the judge, on 500 facts drawn at random each time

claim: After the final pass, 466 of 500 sampled facts were fully supported (the '93%').
quote: Facts fully supported by their mail392 of 500459 of 500466 of 500

claim: No sampled fact was wrong at its core, but about 1 in 15 had a detail a reviewer would soften.
quote: In the last sample, no fact was wrong at its core, but about one in 15 had one detail a careful reviewer would soften

claim: A human blind-graded only 50 of the AI judge's verdicts, agreeing with 48.
quote: A person graded 50 of the third audit's fact verdicts blind and agreed with 48.

claim: Checks cannot tell whether a message was right; a fact is what the mail said.
quote: Neither check can tell whether a message was right. A fact here is what the mail said.

claim: Summary and phase checks are not held out.
quote: The summary and phase checks cover the same pages verification saw, so they aren't held out.

claim: Building and checking cost $11,215 at list prices with no cost optimization.
quote: Building and checking together come to $11,215. We made no attempt to bring that down

claim: Per-unit build cost: 37 cents/message, 18 cents/fact, $41/page.
quote: That's 37 cents a message read, 18 cents a fact and $41 a page

claim: Haiku 4.5 costs a tenth as much but finds about half the facts.
quote: Haiku costs a tenth as much but finds about half the facts

claim: Names and email addresses are published as in the corpus; only phone digits and credentials are masked.
quote: Names and email addresses appear as they do in the corpus.

claim: this+that built the pages with a prototype of its product.
quote: We made these pages with a prototype of something we're building.

claim: Founder says the model kept adding public-record details not in the mail.
quote: The hardest part was that the model already knows Enron. It kept adding details from the public record that the email didn't contain.

claim: Founder cites cost of about $11,000 at list prices, run on a subscription.
quote: about $11,000 at list prices (though we used a subscription)

claim: HN commenter: one incorrect fact could be very damaging for legal/business use.
quote: one incorrect fact could be very damaging and it's very hard to check them all

claim: Founder: product requires humans to approve proposed changes; demo was close to fully automated.
quote: we ask people to approve changes to a company brain that are proposed

claim: Critical HN reaction calling it slop.
quote: A LLM produced tons of irrelevant slop and you're expecting other humans to read it.

claim: Spot check: a cited source mail says Dynegy 'acquired us' on Nov 9, 2001 (the deal later collapsed), showing cited != true.
quote: they inked the deal.  dynegy has aquired us.

claim: Spot check: Dynegy termination fact is backed by a Dow Jones clipping in the mail.
quote: Dynegy Inc. (DYN) terminated its troubled merger agreement with Enron Corp. (ENE), backing away from the deal despite frantic last-minute attempts by both sides to save it.

claim: The underlying CMU corpus has ~150 users and ~0.5M messages released by FERC; CMU asks users to respect privacy.
quote: please be sensitive to the privacy of the people involved
